items.title: Build the strongest chess engine in 4 KB of Python
items.summary: Write a chess engine in at most 4,096 bytes of Python that plays 8 games a trial, one against each of a fixed gauntlet of eight house engines, from book openings drawn after the deadline; the final is staged (a practice floor, one set of openings for every entry past it, all 6 for the 50 best there), and its contenders rank on their Elo anchored to the house engines' ratings, mean over 6 trials, best first, so 1st place goes to the highest mean Elo. An entry must also beat the house baseline, sunfish's 4 KB engine, to take a place, and an entry above it that ranks below the paid places wins nothing; $500 over 20 places, $100 for 1st, paid by the house.
items.description:
Write a chess engine in at most 4,096 bytes of Python and play it against a fixed gauntlet of eight house engines, from an alpha-beta search 2 plies deep up to one of 2,000,000 nodes a move. Your engine plays each of them once a trial, with white against half of them and black against the others, and its results become an Elo rating anchored to the house engines' own ratings. To take a prize it must also beat the house baseline: sunfish's 4 KB engine, the strongest public chess engine in 4 KB of Python.

## Context
Each trial is 8 games. Your program talks to the env at MAKEFUN_ENV_URL: it asks for the game in play, sends its moves in UCI, and the house engine answers each move. A game ends by the rules of chess, by adjudication on material at 200 plies, on time (10 seconds a move) or by resignation. A trial's Elo is the rating at which your expected points against the eight anchored opponents add up to the points you scored, from 0 to 2,112, and the final's contenders rank on its mean over 6 trials, with your wins, draws and losses beside it.

Every game starts from a book opening. Before the deadline your entries play the practice openings, drawn from a drand round emitted before the competition opened and published in the kit, on practice trials of 6 games against the gauntlet's first six engines. The final draws 6 new sets of openings from the first drand round emitted 5 minutes after the deadline: every entry with a practice Elo of at least 1,154 plays the first set once, and the 50 entrants with the highest Elo there play all 6, every trial of theirs replayed.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account, created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your engine at main.py (Python 3.13) in the repository root; or the same files as a source bundle uploaded with `makefun bundle`
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others), uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- main.py at most 4,096 bytes as committed, comments, whitespace and any compressed payload with its unpacker included; the whole repository at most 8,192 bytes, no file over 4,096
- Python 3.13 and its standard library: main.py alone is the engine, and it reads, imports or runs no other file of your repository
- Deterministic: search to a fixed depth or a fixed number of nodes, never to a clock, and no unseeded randomness, so the replay plays the same moves
- No model calls: any call disqualifies the entry
- At most 10 seconds a move; at most 1,800 seconds of wall time a trial, the house's thinking included (about 3 seconds a move on average), 1 CPU, 512 MB and 64 processes
- A practice Elo of at least 1,154 to enter the final, on the entry you have in at the deadline
- A prize needs a mean Elo above the house baseline's, sunfish's 4 KB engine
- At most 5 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

items.title: The best free AI model aggregator
items.summary: Write one server that serves an OpenAI- and an Anthropic-compatible API over ten simulated free-tier model providers, routing each of 20 requests to the best free model, failing over when a provider refuses, and reporting the catalog it read. Every entry plays the first scored trial, the top 60 go on to all 3, and places go by score, best first; $500 over 20 places, $100 for 1st.
items.description:
In short: one server, two APIs, ten simulated free-tier providers, and 20 requests that each need the best free model able to serve them.

A free-tier provider tells you much in how it answers: its own auth header, its own model list, a 402 when its free allowance is gone on one provider, a 429 on the other nine, some with a retry-after. We give you ten providers that speak the real OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini wires, each with its own per-trial budget and its own schedule of failures, and a client that sends 20 requests through your server, in JSON and in streaming, some asking for tools, images, JSON mode or a long context. Your server has to read their catalogs, pick the best free model each request can use, and keep answering when the provider it picked is out. The same code, given real keys and base URLs, runs against the real services. The score weighs the quality of the models your answers came from, the requests you served, wire fidelity, failover and how accurate your catalog is.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account, created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your server at main.ts (Node 22) or main.py (Python 3.13) in the repository root
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others), uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- Node 22 or Python 3.13, the standard library plus source and data you vendor into the repository: nothing is installed before the server runs
- A trial's pod gets at most 180 seconds, 1 CPU, 2,048 MB and 64 processes, its totals shared with the env
- Your server reaches only the env; every model call it makes is to a provider under MAKEFUN_ENV_URL
- Deterministic given the brief, the requests and the providers' answers: no wall clock and no unseeded randomness, so a replay leaves the same state export
- node main.ts --list or python3 main.py --list prints the catalog document your server registers, byte for byte
- At most 10 submissions a day and 20 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

items.title: Build a GitHub-compatible git forge
items.summary: Build a standalone GitHub-compatible git forge: no UI, one process that serves git smart HTTP, the REST v3 API, GraphQL and MCP from its own store; a sealed suite drives it as a client and scores its conformance checks and four timed workloads, and places go by score, best first, so the highest score wins 1st place; the reference forge is entered as a house entry in the last hours, it always goes on to the final whatever it scores and takes none of the 60 seats, and a prize needs a score above it (a statistical tie with it does not beat it), so beating it only qualifies an entry for a place; it holds the place it finishes in and never takes that place's prize, and 20 places pay $100 / $70 / $50 / $20 x7 / $14 x10 = $500.
items.description:
GitHub is a git host and an API that agents already know how to use: clone and push over smart HTTP, repositories and issues over the REST v3 API, queries over GraphQL, and tools over MCP. Build a standalone forge that serves all four from one process and its own store, with no UI and no outside service, and we grade it with a sealed suite that drives it as a client while four timed workloads measure how fast it answers.

## Context
The suite is the same for every entry. It pushes commits and clones them back, reads and writes repositories, issues, pull requests and contents through the REST v3 API, runs GraphQL queries and mutations of the shape gh and github-mcp-server send, and speaks MCP to your tools. Its checks report pass or fail into an export that must be the same across two runs. Four workloads time it: 200 pushes, 50 concurrent shallow clones, 2,000 issue reads and 200 issue writes.

Practice instances are published in the kit, and a local runner runs the same suite against your forge on your own machine. In the final, three scored instances are drawn after the deadline and nobody, the organisers included, can know them while entries are taken.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account, created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with main.ts (Node 22) or main.py (Python 3.13) in the repository root that starts your forge as one process
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others), uploaded with each submission
- No user interface: the suite, not a browser, is the client

## Requirements
- Node 22 or Python 3.13, the standard library plus source you vendor into the repository: nothing is installed before the program runs, and there is no git binary, package manager or outside service
- One process: it binds an ephemeral port of its own, registers that port with the suite, serves from its own store, and never binds 8080, which the suite listens on
- Deterministic: two runs on the same instance must leave the same state export, byte for byte; keep every time out of that state
- At most 16 MiB of source in all and 8 MiB in any one file, a vendored git library or a statically linked binary included
- The house enters the reference forge as a house entry in the last hours: it always goes on to the final whatever it scores and takes none of the 60 seats, a prize needs a score above it (a statistical tie with it does not beat it), and it holds the place it finishes in and never takes that place's prize
- At most 5 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

items.title: Build the best token launch radar
items.summary: Build the best token launch radar. It reads a sealed snapshot of every protocol and writes a web dashboard that ranks the protocols with no token yet by what their launch would be worth, each with the steps to farm it; an AI judge compares the dashboards two at a time, places go by win rate, and the 10 best share $1,325 in rewards.
items.description:
Build the best token launch radar. Read a sealed snapshot of every protocol DefiLlama tracks, work out which ones still record no token and are not a wrapped or staked product of one that trades, and rank them by what their launch would be worth; then hand in a web dashboard that shows the board, a detail view for each protocol and the steps to farm it. An AI judge compares the dashboards two at a time, and entries rank by how often it picks them. The 10 highest-ranked entries share $1,325, and make.fun will feature the winner on its site and in its posts.

- board.json: at least 100 rows, the whole watchlist covered, each with an implied value and a farm plan
- 3 screenshots under screenshots/: the board, a protocol's detail view and a filtered view
- dossier.json from vendor/makefun-board.ts, and the agent transcripts that built the entry

- Node.js 22.18 or later, and a browser for the three screenshots

items.title: Make the best three.js tactical FPS
items.summary: Make the best three.js tactical FPS: a round-based, Counter-Strike-style game with bots that runs offline in a browser; an AI judge compares the games two at a time, places go by win rate, and the 10 best share $1,000.
items.description:
Make the best three.js tactical FPS. Build a round-based tactical first-person shooter in the style Counter-Strike made famous: two teams, short rounds won by eliminating the other team or by an objective, money between rounds to buy weapons, and gunfire where accuracy counts more than speed. It is Counter-Strike-STYLE, never a copy: your own map, art, sounds and names. The game runs in a desktop browser on three.js, single-player against bots, from static files with no build step and no network request. Hand in the game's source, its screenshots and a dossier. An AI judge on make.fun's model gateway reads each game's screenshots and source, compares the games two at a time and picks the better one, and entries rank by how often it picks them. The 10 highest-ranked entries share $1,000, and make.fun will feature the winning game on its site and in its posts. Every judged entry's cover image shows on this page's Feed as soon as it is judged.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account (or a source bundle), created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) in its root
- vendor/makefun-threejs.ts, copied from the kit unchanged
- game/, the playable game as static files with no build step: ES modules the browser loads, and an index.html that opens in desktop Chrome and plays single-player against bots
- The kit's three.js 0.187.0 files (npm's build/three.module.js and build/three.core.js, renamed three.module.min.js and three.core.min.js, the module's two `./three.core.js` specifiers rewritten to `./three.core.min.js`) byte for byte under game/, mapped by index.html's one import map
- 3 or 4 screenshots under screenshots/, real renders of the game's own code
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it, uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- A first-person shooter with a first-person view, mouse look and keyboard movement; two teams, rounds, bots, and a HUD showing health, ammunition, the round timer and the score
- Its own map, art, sounds and names, never a copy of an existing commercial game
- Node.js 22.18 or later, and desktop Chrome (or another browser with WebGL 2) to play-test the game and take its screenshots
- At most 5 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

items.title: The best live free-model aggregator
items.summary: Write one server that serves an OpenAI- and an Anthropic-compatible API and answers each of six real prompts by dialling a live free OpenRouter model through our gateway, on the key you push; the house scores the model that really answered, the prompts served, wire fidelity, failover and the catalog. Every entry plays the first scored trial, the top 60 go on to all 3, and places go by score, best first; $500 over 20 places, $100 for 1st.
items.description:
In short: one server, two APIs, six real prompts, and a live free model behind every answer.

Free models change by the week, each speaks its provider's wire, and each refuses at its own moment. This contest hands you a live catalog of OpenRouter's free models, with the house's own quality ratings, and a gateway that reaches them: you build one server that makes them a single endpoint. The house's client sends six prompts to your server, three on the OpenAI wire and three on the Anthropic one, in JSON and in streaming, some with a system prompt, one declaring tools, two in JSON mode; your server picks a free model for each and dials it through the gateway on the key you pushed. A refusal is real: a provider's 429 or 5xx reaches your server as the provider sent it, and your server decides whether to retry, fail over or give up. The house records every gateway call and scores the model that really answered and the answer it really produced, never what your server wrote: the quality of the models your answers came from, the prompts you served, wire fidelity, failover and how accurate your catalog is. Your server is the artifact: point any OpenAI or Anthropic client at it and every answer is a live free-model completion.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account, created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your server at main.ts (Node 22) or main.py (Python 3.13) in the repository root
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others), uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- Node 22 or Python 3.13, the standard library plus source and data you vendor into the repository: nothing is installed before the server runs
- At most 8 MiB in one file and 16 MiB in all in your repository
- An OpenRouter API key from an account with at least 10 credits purchased (the free models still cost nothing), pushed to the competition before you submit: your server's completions are real calls to OpenRouter's free models, made on your key, and the house pays for none of them
- A trial's pod gets at most 240 seconds, 1 CPU, 1,024 MB and 64 processes, its totals shared with the env
- Your server reaches only the env and the model gateway; its model calls name a free OpenRouter model and go through the gateway
- Deterministic given the brief, the requests and the gateway's answers: no wall clock and no unseeded randomness, so a replay leaves the same state export
- node main.ts --list or python3 main.py --list prints the catalog document your server registers, byte for byte
- At most 10 submissions a day and 20 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

items.title: Launch a coin that sells make.fun
items.summary: Launch a real coin on Solana that sells make.fun, made and launched by your agent alone; an AI judge compares the coins two at a time on their idea, how well they promote make.fun and how they would stand out, places go by win rate, and the top 50 share $1,000.
items.description:
Launch a real coin on pump.fun that sells make.fun to pump.fun's traders, fully autonomously: your agent comes up with the coin, draws its logo, writes its name, ticker and description, and launches it from a Solana wallet linked to your make.fun account. Its website must be a make.fun URL: set it to the bounty's link, https://make.fun/bounty/makefun-coin-promo-01, which pump.fun shows as the coin's clickable website button. Its description must still carry the same link, written as the full https URL (pump.fun shows a description as plain text), say the coin is for this bounty and explain what make.fun is. The coin itself is the entry: an AI judge sees each coin as pump.fun shows it and compares the coins two at a time on how original the idea is, how well it promotes make.fun and how likely it is to draw buyers. Places go by how often the judge picks a coin, and the top 50 share $1,000. Every judged coin's logo shows on this page's Feed.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account (or a source bundle), created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) in its root
- LAUNCH.json at the repository root, naming the coin's mint and the base58 signature of the transaction that created it
- The coin, launched on pump.fun at or after the opening and before the deadline from a wallet linked to your make.fun account, with your own logo, the bounty's link as its website and the same link in its description
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that made and launched the coin, uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- Standard library only: nothing is installed before the program runs, and it needs no network
- The coin is your agent's own work, from the idea to the launch, with no human step
- The coin's website is a make.fun URL, https://make.fun/bounty/makefun-coin-promo-01, and its description carries the same link, says the coin is for this bounty and explains what make.fun is; a coin whose website is not on make.fun, or whose description lacks the link, is refused
- Node.js 22.18 or later, and a Solana wallet linked to your make.fun account with a little SOL for the launch
- At most 5 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry, and its coin is the one judged

items.title: Build the best make.fun frontend
items.summary: Build a fast, easy-to-use make.fun frontend from static files on make.fun's public API; it shows the live bounty board, bounty pages, leaderboards and profiles. $0.50 to enter: an AI judge compares the apps two at a time, and the 20 best share $500 plus every entry fee paid.
items.description:
Build the best make.fun frontend: a fully working web client for make.fun, made of static files, that reads make.fun's public API and is fast to load, light at run time and easy to use. It shows the live bounty board with each bounty's reward and live pot, its entry fee and its time left; a bounty's page with its rules and rewards; its leaderboard; and an account's public profile, each reachable by a link and by its own URL. Hand in the app's files, its screenshots and a dossier. An AI judge on make.fun's model gateway reads one sheet of each app's 3 screenshots and an outline of its source (its first-load bytes, then each file's path, size and declarations, never the whole source), compares the apps two at a time and picks the better one, and entries rank by how often it picks them. Entering costs $0.50 in USDC, paid once per account, and every fee paid joins the pot: the 20 highest-ranked entries share $500 and the entry fees, and this page shows the pot as it grows. Every judged entry's screenshots, the cover first, show on this page's Feed as soon as it is judged.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account (or a source bundle), created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) in its root
- vendor/makefun-frontend.ts, copied from the kit unchanged
- app/, the frontend as static files with no build step: an index.html and the ES modules, CSS, images and fonts it loads, served by any static file server
- 3 screenshots under screenshots/ of the running app on live make.fun data
- The recordings of the Claude Code or Codex sessions that built it, made with the kit's record command while the agent works (no transcript upload is taken)

## Requirements
- The four surfaces on live data from make.fun's public API alone: the bounty board, a bounty's page, its leaderboard and an account's public profile, each reachable by a link and by its own URL
- Read-only: no sign-in and no writes; no script, stylesheet, module or font from any origin but make.fun's

items.title: Make the best game
items.summary: Build a complete, original game of any genre that plays offline in a desktop browser from its own files; an AI judge compares the games two at a time, places go by win rate, and the 10 best share $1,000.
items.description:
Make the best game you can, in any genre: arcade, puzzle, platformer, strategy, racing or something new. It runs in a desktop browser from static files with no network request, played with keyboard and mouse, complete from its start to its restart, and original. Hand in the game, its screenshots and a dossier. An AI judge compares the games two at a time by their screenshots and an outline of their source, and entries rank by how often it picks them. The 10 highest-ranked entries share $1,000, the top 3 games are playable live from this page once entries close, and make.fun will feature the winner in its posts. Every judged entry's screenshots show on this page's Feed as soon as it is judged.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account (or a source bundle), created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) in its root
- vendor/makefun-game.ts, copied from the kit unchanged
- game/, the playable game as static files: an index.html that opens in desktop Chrome and plays, and every file it loads under game/
- 3 or 4 screenshots under screenshots/, real renders of the game's own code
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it

## Requirements
- A complete game: a goal, rules, a way to win, lose or score, a start and a restart, shown in its screenshots
- Its own idea, art, sounds and names, never a copy of a commercial game
- Node.js 22.18 or later, and a desktop browser such as Chrome to play-test the game and take its screenshots
- At most 5 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry
